items.actClause: AN ACT to legalize, validate, ratify and confirm the Penn Yan fire department length of service award program
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3913

TITLE  OF BILL:   An act to legalize, validate, ratify and confirm the
Penn Yan fire department length of service award program

PURPOSE:  This bill would allow volunteer firefighters to  participate
in  various  activities  of the fire department during the course of a
year in order to earn sufficient points to be credited with a year  of
service toward qualifying benefits.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section  1  The  Penn  Yan fire department in 1999 pursuant to article
11-A of the general municipal law, including the adoption of  a  point
system  whereby  volunteer  firefighters  may  participate  during the
course of a year in various activities and earn points to qualify  for
benefits is hereby legalized, validated, ratified and confirmed.

Section 2 The Penn Yan fire department length of service award program
will  have been in full force and effect on and after January 1, 1999,
and volunteer firefighters who have participated in this service award
program during  the  period  beginning  January  1,  1999  and  ending
December  31, 2011 will be credited with points in accordance with the
point system adopted by the village of Penn Yan.

Section 3 This act shall take effect immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:  The Village of Penn Yan created a LOSAP for  the  Penn
Yan  Fire  Department  in  1999  by adopting a resolution creating the
LOSAP and holding a referendum which  ratified  the  creation  of  the
LOSAP.    Although a point system was devised by the fire companies of
the Penn Yan Fire Department the point system was  never  approved  by
the  Board  of  Trustees  until  December 20, 2011, which approval was
required by GML Article 11-A.  The  volunteer  firefighters  performed
their  firefighting  service  with  a good faith expectation that they
would qualify for each annual "year of service" in which,  based  upon
their  participation  in sufficient activities of the Fire Department,
they earned  the  requisite  number  of  points  that  year  for  such
qualifications. It would be an injustice for benefits to be denied any
volunteer  firefighter who, with a good faith expectation of receiving
LOSAP benefits, participated in activities of the Fire Department at a
level to earn years of service, thereby qualifying for LOSAP benefits.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:  2012 - S. 6998, passed Senate, A. 9912, held  in
local government

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to State

EFFECTIVE DATE:  This act shall take effect immediately

A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S3913A

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to legalize, validate, ratify and confirm the
Penn Yan fire department length of service award program

PURPOSE:

This bill would allow volunteer firefighters to participate in various
activities of the fire department during the course of a year in order
to earn sufficient points to be credited with a year of service toward
qualifying benefits.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1 The Penn Yan fire department in 1999 pursuant to article
11-A of the general municipal law, including the adoption of a point
system whereby volunteer firefighters may participate during the
course of a year in various activities and earn points to qualify for
benefits is hereby legalized, validated and confirmed as long as the
fund is currently sufficiently funded to cover the costs of the length
of service award program.

Section 2 The Penn Yan fire department length of service award program
will have been in full force and effect on and after January 1, 1999,
and volunteer firefighters who have participated in this service award
program during the period beginning January 1, 1999 and ending
December 31, 2011 will be credited with points in accordance with the
point system adopted by the village of Penn Yan.

Section 3 This act shall take effect immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:

The Village of Penn Yan created a LOSAP for the Penn Yan Fire
department in 1999 by adopting a resolution creating the LOSAP and
holding a referendum which ratified the creation of of the LOSAP.
Although a point system was devised by the fire companies of the Penn
Yan Fire Department the point system was never approved by the Board
of Trustees until December 20, 2011, which approval was required by
GML Article 11-A. The volunteer firefighters performed their
firefighting service with a good faith expectation that they would
qualify for each annual "year of service" in which, based upon their
participation in sufficient activities of the Fire Department, they
earned the requisite number of points that year for such
qualifications. It would be an injustice for benefits to be denied any
volunteer firefighter who, with a good faith expectation of receiving
LOSAP benefits, participated in activities of the Fire Department at a
level to earn years of service, thereby qualifying for LOSAP benefits.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2013 - S. 3913, referred to local government

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None.


EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.
